Tiny Hat: a new Linux distro dedicated to retro gamedev
stories.summary: Tiny Hat uses only around 100MB of RAM after booting, and can be booted from a >= 1GB memory stick. It comes with a few small games, an easy way to install and run more games and several example programs for getting into retro game development. It also uses a modern stack of libraries, with dwl / Wayland, SDL3 and GTK4. One possible use is to buy a cheap x86 machine for younger members of a family, to completely brain wash inspire them into getting into graphics programming and appreciating retro games, perhaps as a Christmas present. At least a few people have found it fun so far, so I wanted to share it. Comments

stories.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
stories.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.summary: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) Tags: photography , new-york-times , hacker-news , journalism
